newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Court dismisses $6bln suit vs Freeport.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Court dismisses $6bln suit vs Freeport.

text.p: Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc and Freeport-McMoRan Inc said Wednesday a U.S. District Court ruled to dismiss a $6 billion lawsuit alleging human rights and environmental abuses by the companies at some Indonesian operations.
The ruling confirmed that the lawsuit, filed by a New Orleans attorney on behalf of Tom Beanal, an Indonesian tribal leader, had no basis in law, the companies said.

Last April, Amungme tribal leader Beanal filed a suit in the U.S. District Court of New Orleans claiming the company's subsidiary PT Freeport Indonesia had engaged in "eco-terrorism" and "cultural genocide" at its mine in Irian Jaya province.
Beanal said the suit was withdrawn on May 4 because his lawyer filed it without Beanal's consent. The leader then announced plans to reinstate the suit on May 17 after clarifications from his lawyer.

Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold said it planned to continue its work with the local people and the government of Indonesia to implement the government's Integrated Timika Development plan to meet the needs of people in Irian Jaya.

Freeport-McMoRan Copper said it remained committed to working with all groups and parties for the benefit of the indigenous people through educational, health care, job creation and job training programs and infrastructure enhancement programs.
The companies were not immediately available to comment further.
The Freeport mine, some 1,870 miles (3,000 km) east of Jakarta, sits on one of the world's largest known deposits of copper and gold.
On March 12, a Louisiana state court dismissed an identical lawsuit filed on behalf of Yosefa Alomang, also an Indonesian citizen, the companies said.
"The state lawsuit was filed by the same attorney and contained the same baselesss allegations as the dismissed federal lawsuit," they said.
